name: map()
description: Creates a new array by calling a function on every element of the original array, without mutating it.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element. thisArg — optional value to use as `this` inside callback.
returns: A new array with each element being the result of the callback.
notes: map() always returns a new array of the same length — use filter() first if you want to drop elements.

name: filter()
description: Creates a new array containing only the elements that pass a test function.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element, should return true to keep the element.
returns: A new array with the elements that passed the test; empty array if none did.

name: reduce()
description: Reduces an array to a single value by applying a function against an accumulator and each element, left to right.
parameters: callback — receives the running accumulator and the current element. initialValue — starting value for the accumulator.
returns: The final accumulated value.
notes: Without an initialValue, the first array element is used as the initial accumulator and iteration starts from the second element.

name: forEach()
description: Executes a function once for each array element. Used for side effects rather than producing a new value.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element. thisArg — optional value to use as `this`.
returns: undefined — forEach() always returns undefined, unlike map().
notes: Cannot be stopped early with break; use a for...of loop or some()/every() if you need early exit.

name: find()
description: Returns the first element in the array that satisfies the provided test function.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element until it returns truthy.
returns: The first matching element, or undefined if none match.
notes: Stops iterating as soon as a match is found, unlike filter() which checks every element.

name: findIndex()
description: Returns the index of the first element that satisfies the provided test function.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element until it returns truthy.
returns: The index of the first matching element, or -1 if none match.

name: some()
description: Tests whether at least one element in the array passes the provided test function.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element until it returns truthy.
returns: true if any element passes the test, otherwise false. Returns false for empty arrays.
notes: Short-circuits — stops iterating as soon as a truthy result is found.

name: every()
description: Tests whether all elements in the array pass the provided test function.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element until it returns falsy.
returns: true if every element passes the test, otherwise false. Returns true for empty arrays.
notes: Short-circuits — stops iterating as soon as a falsy result is found.

name: includes()
description: Determines whether an array contains a certain value, returning true or false.
parameters: searchElement — value to search for. fromIndex — optional index to start searching from.
returns: Boolean indicating whether the value was found.
notes: Unlike indexOf(), includes() correctly detects NaN using SameValueZero comparison.

name: indexOf()
description: Returns the first index at which a given element can be found in the array, or -1 if not present.
parameters: searchElement — value to locate. fromIndex — optional index to start searching from.
returns: The index of the first match, or -1 if not found.
notes: Uses strict equality (===) and cannot find NaN — use includes() for that case.

name: lastIndexOf()
description: Returns the last index at which a given element can be found, searching the array backwards.
parameters: searchElement — value to locate. fromIndex — optional index to start searching backward from.
returns: The index of the last match, or -1 if not found.

name: push()
description: Adds one or more elements to the end of an array and mutates the original array.
parameters: item1, item2, ... — elements to append.
returns: The new length of the array.
notes: Mutates the array in place — use the spread operator ([...a, 3]) for an immutable version.

name: pop()
description: Removes the last element from an array and returns it, mutating the original array.
returns: The removed element, or undefined if the array was empty.

name: shift()
description: Removes the first element from an array and returns it, mutating the original array and shifting remaining elements down.
returns: The removed element, or undefined if the array was empty.
notes: O(n) operation since every remaining element must be re-indexed — avoid in hot loops on large arrays.

name: unshift()
description: Adds one or more elements to the beginning of an array and mutates the original array.
parameters: item1, item2, ... — elements to prepend.
returns: The new length of the array.

name: splice()
description: Changes the contents of an array by removing, replacing, or adding elements in place.
parameters: start — index to begin changing. deleteCount — number of elements to remove. item1... — elements to insert.
returns: An array containing the deleted elements.
notes: Mutates the original array — use slice() if you need a non-mutating alternative.

name: slice()
description: Returns a shallow copy of a portion of an array, from start up to (but not including) end, without mutating the original.
parameters: start — index to begin extraction (default 0). end — index to stop before (default array length).
returns: A new array containing the extracted elements.
notes: Negative indices count from the end of the array.

name: concat()
description: Merges two or more arrays into a new array, without mutating any of the originals.
parameters: array2, array3, ... — arrays or values to merge in.
returns: A new array combining all the elements.
notes: The spread operator ([...a, ...b]) is a commonly used alternative for merging arrays.

name: join()
description: Joins all elements of an array into a single string, separated by the given separator.
parameters: separator — optional string to insert between elements (default is a comma).
returns: A string with all array elements joined.

name: sort()
description: Sorts the elements of an array in place according to a compare function, or as strings by default.
parameters: compareFn — optional function (a, b) => number; negative sorts a first, positive sorts b first.
returns: The same array, sorted in place.
notes: Without a compareFn, elements are converted to strings and sorted lexicographically — [10, 1, 21].sort() gives [1, 10, 21] wrong; always pass a compareFn for numbers.

name: reverse()
description: Reverses the order of the elements of an array in place.
returns: The same array, with elements reversed.
notes: Mutates the original array — use [...array].reverse() to avoid mutating.

name: flat()
description: Creates a new array with all sub-array elements concatenated into it up to the specified depth.
parameters: depth — how deep to flatten nested arrays (default 1). Use Infinity to flatten fully.
returns: A new, flattened array.

name: flatMap()
description: Maps each element using a mapping function, then flattens the result by one level into a new array.
parameters: callback — function invoked per element, may return an array to be flattened.
returns: A new array with the mapped and flattened results.
notes: Equivalent to map() followed by flat(1), but slightly more efficient.

name: Array.from()
description: Creates a new array instance from an array-like or iterable object, such as a NodeList, string, or Set.
parameters: arrayLike — object with a length property or an iterable. mapFn — optional function applied to each element.
returns: A new Array instance.
notes: Commonly used to convert NodeLists, Sets, or Maps into real arrays so array methods can be used.

name: Array.isArray()
description: Determines whether the passed value is an Array.
parameters: value — the value to test.
returns: true if the value is an array, otherwise false.
notes: More reliable than typeof for detecting arrays, since typeof [] === 'object'.
